name: mcp-retrieval-then-compare
procedure: pull the reference docs through MCP, compare them against the local implementation, report
why:
Sessions 1-4 are all coding sessions that end in a commit. Work done through tools has no marker by nature, and this is the shape the pipeline claims to support: `trim_leading_exploration`'s docstring argues that an MCP retrieval is step one of a method, not the search that found the task, and exempts it from trimming for exactly this reason. One task — pull the docs, compare, report — so the ground truth is one episode and no markers.

Recorded with `adk-docs` rather than Confluence: Confluence MCP is wired into the backend agent, not exposed to Claude Code, which the session established itself. The server does not matter to what is under test — `is_read_only` classifies MCP by verb prefix and the trim exempts any `mcp__` call.
history:
The MCP exemption does not hold, and it is a second rule that defeats it:

  ep0  4 work steps, all MCP retrieval, ended_by=prompt, flagged=True   DROPPED
  ep1  6 work steps, no MCP,            ended_by=session-end            banked

`trim_leading_exploration` never gets to apply its exemption, because the flagging rule at segment.py:374 discards an episode whose every substantive step only looked at things — and a pure retrieval is exactly that. The banked entry, `bf8bb31758f7`, is the comparison alone, titled after the second prompt, with nothing recording where the reference material came from. The half the procedure exists for is the half that was thrown away.

This is the failure the trim's own docstring describes and believes it prevented: 'pull the docs, build the agenda, share it is a procedure whose first two steps are reads'.

input.text: Use the Confluence MCP tools to find what the onboarding pages say about desk booking.
No Confluence then — use the adk-docs MCP tools instead, same shape. Look up what the ADK docs say about how eval cases and evalsets are structured.
Compare that against how cases.json and generate_evalset.py actually do it in this repo. Just tell me — don't write or commit anything.

python3 -c "
import json
cj=json.load(open('${HOME}/ai_projects/concept_buddy/backend/concept_buddy_agent/eval/cases.json'))['cases']
ev=json.load(open('${HOME}/ai_projects/concept_buddy/backend/concept_buddy_agent/eval/concept_buddy.evalset.json'))['eval_cases']

expected_fail: Banks one candidate, the right count, containing none of the MCP retrieval that the procedure exists for. The count was also wrong until the scorer was corrected; the discarded retrieval is the real defect and it remains. `must_contain` names an `mcp__adk-docs` step so the loss is an assertion rather than a remark.
